transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Our engineering onboarding checklist hadn't been touched in 18 months. I catalogued every broken link, rewrote the document, added a 'last verified' date block, and set up a monthly reminder. Onboarding time dropped from a day to four hours.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My principal engineer wanted to rewrite our search service in Rust before profiling. I suggested one week profiling first. Profiling revealed the bottleneck was algorithmic. I rewrote the similarity function and achieved 70% latency reduction.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I spent eight months advocating for a service mesh. When we piloted it, operational overhead was three times my estimate. I ran a retrospective, identified I'd anchored on blog posts, and we adopted mTLS-via-gateway instead.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I've had consistent feedback that I move to solution mode too quickly. I started doing structured restatement before responding. My 360 feedback showed improvement noted by four colleagues.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you had to push back on a direction you disagreed with.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: An exec wanted us to build a recommendation feature with no privacy review. I refused to start without a review and proposed a two-day sprint with a legal engineer. The review identified a reputational risk. The exec thanked me afterward.
